name: hypertension treatment overview
title: Hypertension treatment decision chart: treat once blood pressure is over the threshold for the patient's risk, start one drug or a low-dose two-drug pill depending on the distance from target, then build the cocktail in steps (RAAS inhibitor, a diuretic and a calcium channel blocker, then spironolactone, beta blocker or doxazosin), each class with when to choose it and when to avoid it

nodes.title: Hypertension above the threshold for this patient's RISK: which drugs, in what order?
lines: START → TARGET (mmHg): HIGH risk systolic ≥ 130 → ≤ 120 · DIABETES ≥ 130/80 → < 130/80
healthy behaviours for everyone · ≤ 10 mmHg above target: ONE drug · > 10 mmHg: TWO drugs as a low-dose single pill
not at target: ADD a drug, don't double one (half dose gives 80% of the effect)
pair a renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) INHIBITOR with a STIMULATOR

nodes.title: STEP 1: a RAAS inhibitor
lines: will they COUGH on an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor?

nodes.title: STEPS 2–3: a diuretic or a calcium channel blocker (CCB), then the other
lines: both STIMULATE the RAAS: choose by K+ and pedal edema

nodes.title: STEP 4: the 4th drug
lines: choose by K+ and heart rate

nodes.title: ACE inhibitor or ARB
lines: perindopril, trandolapril; angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB): telmisartan, candesartan

nodes.title: Thiazide-like diuretic
lines: indapamide, chlorthalidone
longer-acting: preferred over thiazides

nodes.title: Long-acting CCB
lines: dihydropyridine: amlodipine, nifedipine

nodes.title: Spironolactone
lines: mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA)

nodes.title: Beta blocker or doxazosin
lines: bisoprolol; doxazosin is an alpha-1 blocker

nodes.title: Compelling indications
lines: • ischemic heart disease (+ beta blocker)
• left ventricular dysfunction, non-diabetic kidney disease
• diabetes with neuropathy: ARB

nodes.title: ACE cough
lines: switch to an ARB

nodes.title: First line, or with the RAAS inhibitor
lines: • cerebrovascular disease
• step 6: K+ > 3.7 → MORE diuretic

nodes.title: First line, or with the RAAS inhibitor
lines: • cerebrovascular disease
• preferred 3-drug cocktail: + diuretic + ACE inhibitor or ARB

nodes.title: Step 4, if the K+ allows
lines: • step 6: K+ < 3.7 → MORE spironolactone

nodes.title: Beta blocker
lines: • ischemic heart disease, recent ST-elevation MI
• a fast heart rate at step 4

nodes.title: NO in pregnancy or renovascular disease
lines: • caution if she could become pregnant
• renovascular: high K+, worse kidneys

nodes.title: Not ALONE in Black patients
lines: low-renin hypertension: start a renin stimulator

nodes.title: Diuretic-induced LOW K+
lines: pair with an ACE inhibitor or ARB (they spare K+)

nodes.title: Diuretic + CCB: the SAME column
lines: add a RAAS inhibitor; monitor electrolytes

nodes.title: Two RAAS inhibitors together
lines: monitor electrolytes (K+)

nodes.title: Beta blocker NOT first line at ≥ 60
lines: unless angina or heart failure

nodes.title: On all 4 drugs and still NOT at target? Very exceptional, or not taking them
lines: • adherence aids: blister packs, a daily routine, home BP readings
• DIRECTLY OBSERVED: watch all 4 taken in clinic on an ambulatory BP monitor
• step 6, poor kidney function → a renal-impairment algorithm
